stories.headline: AP moves to capture flood surge as reservoirs gain 21 TMC
stories.title: AP moves to capture flood surge as reservoirs gain 21 TMC
stories.summary: Naidu seeks Centre’s nod for new barrages Orders maximum diversion of rising river flows 29 reservoirs across state record sharp gains Vamsadhara, Nagavali, Godavari, Krishna in spate Announces 50 kg free rice for affected fishermen
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Amaravati: The state government is moving to capture the surge in river flows triggered by heavy rains, with storage in 29 reservoirs rising by about 21 TMC in three days even as several districts face inundation and crop damage.

Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu, who reviewed the flood and rainfall situation with senior officials through a teleconference on Saturday, directed the authorities to make maximum use of the additional water while continuing relief and rescue operations.
The combined storage in 29 reservoirs increased from 101 TMC on September 23 by around 21 TMC by September 26.

Of this, 11 projects in North Andhra gained about 5 TMC, while 18 reservoirs in Kakinada, Polavaram, Alluri Sitarama Raju, Eluru, Palnadu, Nellore, Kurnool, Kadapa and Anantapur districts recorded another 16 TMC.
The sharpest increases were reported in North Andhra.
Inflows into Gotta Barrage in the Vamsadhara basin rose from 7,214 cusecs on September 20 to 47,100 cusecs on September 25.

At Narayanapuram Anicut in the Nagavali basin, inflows surged from 2,100 to 49,800 cusecs, while Madduvvalasa Project saw inflows rise from 918 to nearly 18,000 cusecs, lifting storage from 1.61 TMC to 2.79 TMC.
Inflows at Thotapalli Barrage increased from 2,484 to about 23,250 cusecs.
In the Godavari basin, Donkarayi storage rose from 11.67 TMC to 15.78 TMC and Seeleru reservoir storage from 1.52 TMC to 3.90 TMC.
Dowleswaram flows increased from 1.20 lakh to 3.50 lakh cusecs.
In the Krishna basin, Prakasam Barrage inflows rose from 8,187 to 40,521 cusecs, while Munneru flows increased from 3,210 to 9,000 cusecs.
Naidu directed officials to fill small and medium water bodies wherever possible and to divert available water into reservoirs.

stories.headline: Flood Fury In State: Fields under water, villages cut off
stories.title: Flood Fury In State: Fields under water, villages cut off
stories.summary: Crops in 43,803 hectares inundated across 12 districts 69,258 farmers in 1,216 villages may lose standing crops Nagavali blankets Srikakulam farmlands with a vast sheet of water
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Amaravati: For thousands of families across Andhra Pradesh, the current flooding is no longer just a story of swollen rivers and overflowing fields; it represents the loss of months of labour, livelihoods, and the destruction of hard-won harvest on which they had pinned their hopes.

Farmers who struggled through inadequate rainfall during the Kharif season are now watching standing crops disappear under floodwater, while families in river-island and low-lying villages are finding roads and access routes cut off.
The scale of the calamity is discernible in the preliminary assessment.

Heavy rains and floods have inundated 43,802.83 hectares of agricultural land across 12 districts, affecting 69,258 farmers in 1,216 villages spread over 185 mandals, according to the Preliminary Crop Damage Report as of September 26.
The loss on the farm front is particularly stark in Srikakulam, where the Nagavali has spilled far beyond its banks.
An inflow of about 70,000 cusecs pushed floodwater across thousands of acres, with water carpeting nearly 20 km.
In several fields, there is knee-deep water.
Around 15 villages, including Korlakota, Chimalavalasa and Kothapeta, have vast stretches of paddy under water, while roads connecting villages have also been submerged.
For these farmers, the disaster has come after an already difficult season.
The source report records that they had struggled initially with inadequate rainfall and water availability and had managed to raise the Kharif crop with difficulty.
Now, with the crop approaching harvest, floodwaters have wiped out the results of herculean efforts.
Farmers in Amudalavalasa are seeking immediate field inspections and compensation, with several villages reporting completely submerged fields.

stories.headline: CPI leader Binoy Viswam demands Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation over alleged BJP ties
stories.title: CPI leader Binoy Viswam demands Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation over alleged BJP ties
stories.summary: This comes after former Kerala Chief Secretary Jiji Thomson claimed that Gyanesh Kumar urged him to contest Parliamentary elections on a BJP ticket in 2016.
reasons: source: event has 3 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: 3 independent source groups -> high confidence
article_sentences: Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar’s total subservience to the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has been exposed fully, following the startling revelation by the former Chief Secretary, Jiji Thomson, the State secretary of CPI, Binoy Viswam has said.

Mr. Thomson had earlier alleged that during his tenure as the Chief Secretary, Mr. Kumar had once asked him why he did not contest Parliamentary elections on a BJP ticket, saying he could have become a Union Minister.
According to Mr. Thomson, the conversation had happened in 2016, while the two were travelling on the same flight to New Delhi.

In a statement here, Mr. Viswam said that by offering the lure of a Union Minister’s post under the BJP to a senior civil servant in Keralam, Mr. Kumar has proved that he is someone who is willing to stoop to any level for the BJP.
He said Mr. Kumar later headed the infamous Ayodhya Trust and that the BJP is using the same person to crush democracy for Amit Shah, Mr. Viswam added.
He alleged that Mr. Kumar had been made the CEC as a reward for all the intrigues he has carried out on behalf of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Mr. Shah.
Mr. Kumar’s conduct has now become unacceptable even to the other Election Commissioners, he stated.
Mr. Kumar has robbed 13 crore Indians of their right to vote and is a disgrace to the world’s largest democracy.
All democratic-minded Indians now believe that elections can never be free and fair under such an individual, Mr. Viswam claimed.
He demanded that Mr. Kumar should resign from the CEC post immediately if he retained even a shred of loyalty to the Constitution or that he would have to surrender before mounting public fury.
Mr. Viswam added that after Mr. Kumar’s exit, the Electronic Voting Machines too need to exit Indian democracy.

stories.headline: Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi | Dissent in the Election Commission
stories.title: Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi | Dissent in the Election Commission
stories.summary: The two Election Commissioner, both appointed by the government under the new 2023 law, have raised questions about changes to electoral rolls, centralised control and the Election Commission’s decision-making process
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: When notices began to be issued after the publication of the draft list during the Delhi SIR [special intensive revision], one of the names was that of Election Commissioner (EC) Sukhbir Singh Sandhu.

What was considered ironical on that day and time soon became a moment of reckoning for the poll body as reports emerged that Dr. Sandhu, along with his fellow Election Commissioner Vivek Joshi, had flagged many anomalies in the ongoing SIR process across the country over the last 10 months.

Though rumours of a rift within the Election Commission of India had been doing the rounds for some months, what came as a surprise were the formal dissent notes written by the two ECs, including one to the Cabinet Secretary, as both had been virtually handpicked by the government under the new 2023 Law for Appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners.
The Opposition Congress party had given written objections during the appointment of both in the selection committee meetings.

When Dr. Sandhu was appointed along with CEC Gyanesh Kumar on March 14, 2024, following the retirement of EC Anup Chandra Pandey and the abrupt resignation of EC Arun Goel, Congress leader Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury had given a formal dissent note in the selection committee.
Later, when Mr. Joshi was appointed on February 17, 2025 after Gyanesh Kumar was elevated to CEC, Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi raised objection in the committee meeting.
Both the Election Commissioners had reportedly flagged several key issues, including the centralisation of the Electoral Rolls.
In May this year, Mr. Joshi proposed an audit to certify that “no one except the concerned statutory authorities has any credentials to make any change in the (voter) database”.

In August, Dr. Sandhu recorded that State-level election officials were reporting that they do not have “proper and complete access” to the ERONet portal — the digital system through which the electoral rolls are maintained.

He further flagged that Election Commission Director General of IT “does not have any legal authority to restrict proper and complete access and freedom to operate as given by law to the statutory authorities”.
The two ECs also said that Form 6 — which new voters must fill to register— was altered to ask if the applicant or their parents/grandparents “exist” in the electoral roll of the last SIR.

They warned as early as May that such a statutory form cannot be changed without amending the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, and Dr. Sandhu called the change “unauthorised and illegal” in August, demanding its immediate removal.

stories.headline: Election Commission on SIR row: Agendas to be shared before meetings, minutes to follow
stories.title: Election Commission on SIR row: Agendas to be shared before meetings, minutes to follow
stories.summary: The Commission maintained that its decisions relating to the SIR exercise were taken with the approval of all three Election Commissioners
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Election Commission of India (ECI) on Saturday announced new measures to bring greater procedural transparency to its functioning amid the ongoing controversy over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
The poll panel said agendas for all Commission meetings will now be circulated in advance, while minutes of the meetings will be issued after deliberations.
The decision came at a meeting chaired by Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at Nirvachan Sadan in New Delhi, attended by Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi.

The meeting followed reports alleging that Sandhu and Joshi had raised objections on record at least 14 times over the past 10 months regarding aspects of the SIR exercise and the functioning of the poll panel.
Addressing the controversy, the ECI said the June 24, 2025 order for conducting SIR across all states and Union Territories was approved unanimously by all three commissioners.
The Commission also said the SIR schedules issued subsequently for 12 States/UTs and another 19 States/UTs received unanimous approval.
The poll panel further stated that differences in views and observations are part of institutional deliberations and maintained that its orders have legal sanction and follow statutory procedures.

The ECI also clarified that letters sent by Sandhu and Joshi to the Cabinet Secretary concerned the functioning of an officer deputed to the Commission and were not related to any policy matter or the functioning of its.
IT division.
The SIR exercise has emerged as one of the largest electoral-roll revision exercises in recent years.

According to reports, more than 13 crore names were struck off draft electoral rolls across 30 States and Union Territories during the exercise, intensifying scrutiny over the process of additions, deletions and voter verification.

In Delhi, the Supreme Court recently questioned the manner in which notices were issued to voters, with more than 33 lakh voters receiving notices over issues including alleged “logical discrepancies”.
